Subject: Cynddelw Llythfor, a 42-year-old ordinary Cenyri human male newspaper reporter in a medieval Celtic fantasy port. Chest-up portrait with both hands clearly visible. Straight medium brown hair swept neatly backwards beneath a casual soft dark olive wool cap worn back enough to show the hairline. A cheeky tidy pointed short brown beard and slim curled moustache, intelligent slightly tired face, warm hazel eyes. He hugs a small worn brown leather notebook to his chest with his left hand and rests his right hand thoughtfully on his chin. His eyes look dreamily and pensively up towards the sky, eyebrows slightly raised; charming earnest thoughtful expression, not buffoonish. Ordinary comfortable layered clothing: open brown wool waistcoat over a cream linen shirt, muted blue neckcloth, affordable well-kept clothes. Quiet softly simplified background of Gwynthor's timber and stone street with a glimpse of pale sky; one person only, restrained composition. Normal rounded human ears. No modern items, no glasses, no writing, no logos, no frame. This is a new man, not a gender swap of the reference.

Upper-body portrait, hands loosely folded at waist; relaxed confident posture and a slight playful head tilt, gaze towards viewer. Subtle out-of-focus Gwynthor timber-window background with daylight. One person only, normal rounded human ears, no nobility crowns or opulent jewelry, no text, no frame. She is not the same person as the reference and not a child.

Reference 1 defines drawing style and cel-shaded world; reference 2 defines Rhyfel horse anatomy ONLY, not its rendering style or mane.
Subject: Trötzli, a powerful adult male Rhyfel warhorse in the prime of life, approximately eight years old. Entire horse including all four shaggy feathered feet visible with breathing room, three-quarter side view. Light tan beige-brown coat, broad deep chest, muscular heavy neck, strong angular head, solid sturdy legs and broad hooves; healthy and well nourished, never thin or elderly. Wary exhausted-looking expression, tense high neck, one ear turned back and the other listening forward, alert worried eyes and slightly flared nostrils. Many clearly visible OLD fully healed pale scars: curved bite marks, smooth irregular old burn patches, long healed spear/sword scars, small healed arrow puncture marks and several parallel healed claw scratches across shoulder, flank and neck. All scars closed and mature, no blood, no open wounds, no gore. Very short trimmed dark sandy mane in close neat military braids along the crest, no long flowing mane. Tail hair kept short to about hock level and tightly braided, military utilitarian cut, anatomically normal tail. Heavy feathering around the lower legs. A plain soft leather halter without a lead rope is fine; NO saddle, armor, rider, weapons or heraldry. Quiet simple paddock background with a plain fence in soft daylight, no other animals or people. Calm but visibly guarded standing posture, not rearing, no comic grin, no magical effects, no text, no frame.

Keep all scars closed and mature without blood. Change anatomy and the hard muscle shading only.

Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: an in-world child's drawing to be pinned to a medieval fantasy help notice, portrait sheet 2:3.
IMPORTANT: This is deliberately the naive hand-drawn sketch made by Eirlys, an eight-year-old daughter, NOT a polished anime illustration, not a professional cartoon, not a realistic portrait. The references ONLY identify the horse and her father. Translate their recognisable traits into very simple awkward child drawings.
On a warm cream sheet of rough paper, an eight-year-old has drawn in uneven charcoal, brown pencil and a few rubbed ochre and blue chalk patches: Trötzli, a light tan/beige-brown sturdy horse with a few old scar scribbles, short zigzag braided mane, short braided tail and shaggy feet, stands on the left. He is kicking one hind leg backwards. To the right, her father Cynddelw in a floppy olive cap, little pointed brown beard, brown waistcoat and blue neckcloth, recoils in exaggerated shock. The raised hoof passes just beside his head WITHOUT hitting him. His arms fly up, eyes wide, mouth a surprised O; his cap tilts or flies slightly upwards. Clear funny near-miss, no injury, no gore.
Childlike uneven lines, flat simple shapes, wobbly perspective, disproportionate head and limbs, stray construction lines, rubbed smudges and a few scribbled motion marks. Sparse simple drawing with lots of paper visible. Small clumsy handwritten labels exactly 'Trötzli' beside the horse and 'Papi' beside the father. At the bottom one tiny childlike credit 'Eirlys'. No elaborate scene or background, only a crooked ground line. Both figures and all extremities fully visible, no frame, no seal, no modern pencils pictured, no adult calligraphy. Must look convincingly drawn by a child, affectionate and funny rather than threatening.
